title: The Consummate Constitutionalist
primary_topics: Exordium (Latin for Introduction) to Justice Adolfo S. Azcuna's autobiography, written August 18-27, 2022

The case for calling Justice Azcuna 'The Consummate Constitutionalist': constitution maker (1971 ConCon and 1986 ConCom), constitution implementer (Chief Presidential Legal Counsel and other roles under Cory), and constitution interpreter (SC Associate Justice)

Three highlights from the autobiography: (1) the 'lawyer as someone who helps the judge find out what really happened' (from Azcuna's daughter Rina); (2) the simplified EEZ definition; (3) the Bayan v. Ermita decision creating freedom parks
CJP's personal role in the P300-million Japanese government grant that funded the PHILJA Training Center in Tagaytay
sub_topics: Autobiography: '8th (and final) softcopy, Aug. 6, 2022, 50,265 words' with Foreword by Justice Tony Carpio; CJP read it in six hours over the weekend of August 20-21
Assessment: 'simple and graspable; humble and palpable; never haughty or naughty or deprecating, yet no less ennobling and enabling'

Rina's definition of a lawyer (pages 82-83): 'A LAWYER IS SOMEONE WHO HELPS THE JUDGE FIND OUT WHAT REALLY HAPPENED' -- said after watching a trial in Pasig; CJP calls it 'the best definition of a lawyer'

EEZ definition (pages 134-136): not part of territory; portion of high seas; sovereign rights but not sovereignty; 200 nautical miles seaward; UNCLOS governs; subject to freedoms of high seas (except fishing); sharing obligation if fish resources exceed capacity

1971 ConCon: Azcuna won as delegate for Lone District of Zamboanga del Norte at age 32; four pet proposals -- integrate the Philippine Bar, territorial citizen's army, continental shelf in territory delineation, writ of Amparo; first three succeeded; Amparo had to wait for the 1987 Constitution

1986 ConCom: one of 48 members; named ConCom dramatis personae -- former CJs Concepcion and Davide; ConCom President Munoz-Palma; Senators Padilla, Rodrigo, Sumulong, Rosales, Speaker Laurel Jr.; religious leaders Bishop Bacani, Fr. Bernas, Sr. Christine Tan, Rev. Rigos; Muslim leaders Alonto, Uka, Abubakar; lawyers Felicitas Aquino, Jamir, Romulo, Colayco, Regalado, Nolledo, Bengzon, Monsod, Maambong, Sarmiento; Blas Ople; Azcuna as consummately adept in shaping the 1987 Constitution
1987 Constitution: over 35 years later, intact (warts included) -- 'a record here and in many countries'

Chief Presidential Legal Counsel and other Cory roles: advised Cory she was not barred from running for presidency in 1992 but Cory graciously declined and pushed FVR over Mitra; surviving coup attempts; Cory's US/Canada/France/Germany/other country visits

Failed 1992 Senate campaign: ran at Cory's urging on FVR ticket; FVR won but Azcuna lost; returned to practice at Azcuna, Yorac, Sarmiento, Arroyo and Chua Law Office; praised William T. Chua as 'life and soul of our partnership'

SC Associate Justice (appointed by GMA October 20, 2002): adjusted to collegial Court; mentoring by senior justices; decision-making processes; Azcuna vs. Carpio debate with 'international repercussions'
Bayan v. Ermita: CJP calls it Azcuna's most remarkable decision -- creation of 'freedom parks, either real or constructive, all over the country'
PHILJA Chancellor: 6 two-year terms = 12 years (until May 31, 2021); SC term totals 9 years in Court proper + 12 years in PHILJA

P300 million Japanese grant: CJP's personal role as CJ -- told Japanese Ambassador Ryuichiro Yamamoto he had 'excess' P300M; CJP requested it for PHILJA Training Center; January 18, 2006 check handed to CJP in SC Session Hall; passed to Justice Ameurfina Melencio-Hererra (Azcuna's predecessor as PHILJA Chancellor)

stances.claim: Justice Azcuna is 'The Consummate Constitutionalist' because he uniquely holds all three constitutional distinctions simultaneously: constitution maker (1971 ConCon and 1986 ConCom), constitution implementer (Chief Presidential Legal Counsel and other Cory-era roles), and constitution interpreter (SC Associate Justice). Very few anywhere can claim all three.
stances.rhetorical_move: triple-distinction argument: the three roles combine into a unique constitutional completeness that no one else holds

stances.claim: The 1987 Constitution -- now over 35 years old and intact (warts included) -- is 'certainly a record here and in many countries,' a testament to the quality of work done by the 1986 ConCom despite attempts to revise it.
stances.rhetorical_move: longevity-as-quality-proof: the Constitution's durability is the retrospective validation of the ConCom's craft

stances.claim: The best definition of a lawyer -- 'someone who helps the judge find out what really happened' -- was formulated not by a legal scholar but by Rina Azcuna as a little girl watching a trial in Pasig. CJP calls it 'the best definition of a lawyer,' better than anything in legal literature.
stances.rhetorical_move: child-wisdom-as-ultimate-definition: the non-lawyer's intuition as superior to professional formulations
stances.confidence: asserted as CJP's personal judgment -- 'same for me, Justice Adolf'

stances.claim: Bayan v. Ermita -- creating 'freedom parks, either real or constructive, all over the country' -- is Azcuna's most remarkable decision because it translated constitutional liberty from an abstract guarantee into a tangible, nationwide physical reality.
stances.rhetorical_move: abstraction-to-reality test: the decision's value measured by its creation of concrete civic spaces
stances.confidence: asserted as CJP's opinion ('to me, however'...)

notable_anecdotes: The 6:51 AM SMS: CJP received Azcuna's request for an Exordium by SMS at 6:51 AM on August 18, 2022; replied after his morning stroll with Leni ('Wow, it's 271 pages. Please give me the weekend...'); read it in six hours over August 20-21.

Rina's lawyer definition: during a trial in Pasig that her father brought her to (school was cancelled), little Rina watched a witness examination and told her father: 'Papa, I now know what a lawyer is... A LAWYER IS SOMEONE WHO HELPS THE JUDGE FIND OUT WHAT REALLY HAPPENED.' Justice Azcuna calls it the best definition; CJP agrees: 'same for me, Justice Adolf.'

EEZ from a child's perspective (sort of): Azcuna's pages 134-136 simplified the EEZ -- 'not, strictly speaking, part of our territory... sovereign rights are short of sovereignty because they do not include ownership of the territory but only exclusive right to its resources.'

The 1971 Amparo failure and 1987 success: Azcuna wanted to include the writ of Amparo in the 1971 Constitution; only Davide and Noli Santos understood it; it was not adopted. In 1987, with Concepcion's advice -- 'leave the Bill of Rights alone; insert it in the powers of the Supreme Court' -- it finally made it into Art. VIII on Judicial Power.

The P300M Japanese grant: CJP told Japanese Ambassador Yamamoto he had 'excess' funds; CJP immediately cited the PHILJA Training Center need; January 18, 2006, the Ambassador handed CJP a P300M check at a ceremony at the SC Session Hall; CJP passed it to Justice Melencio-Hererra.
CJP's prediction for Azcuna: 'I will look forward to calling him the Consummate Hubby, Dad and Lolo ten years from now when I pray I would still be around even in a wheelchair.'

one_paragraph_summary: Written August 18-27, 2022 as the Exordium (Latin for Introduction) to Justice Adolfo S. Azcuna's autobiography, this piece by CJP opens with the 6:51 AM SMS: Azcuna asked CJP to 'do me the honor of an Exordium'; CJP read the 50,265-word, 271-page final draft in six hours over the August 20-21 weekend. CJP describes the autobiography as 'simple and graspable; humble and palpable; never haughty or naughty or deprecating, yet no less ennobling and enabling,' and argues for calling Azcuna 'The Consummate Constitutionalist' -- a title justified by three simultaneous distinctions: constitution maker (1971 ConCon delegate for Lone District of Zamboanga del Norte, age 32, where four of his proposals -- bar integration, citizen's army, continental shelf, and the writ of Amparo -- were debated; the first three passed but Amparo had to wait for the 1987 Constitution, where with Concepcion's advice it was inserted into Art. VIII on Judicial Power); constitution implementer (Chief Presidential Legal Counsel, Press Secretary, and other Cory-era roles -- surviving coup attempts, advising Cory she could run in 1992 but would graciously decline); and constitution interpreter (SC Associate Justice, appointed by GMA October 20, 2002). CJP highlights three passages from the book: Rina Azcuna's child-definition of a lawyer ('A LAWYER IS SOMEONE WHO HELPS THE JUDGE FIND OUT WHAT REALLY HAPPENED' -- 'the best definition of a lawyer,' CJP agrees); the simplified EEZ explanation (pages 134-136: sovereign rights but not sovereignty, 200 nautical miles, UNCLOS-governed); and Bayan v. Ermita -- 'his most remarkable decision' -- creating 'freedom parks, either real or constructive, all over the country.' CJP also recalls his personal role in securing the P300-million no-strings Japanese government grant for the PHILJA Training Center in Tagaytay (January 18, 2006, check presented by Ambassador Yamamoto at the SC Session Hall). The Exordium closes: 'We never retire. We just change tires for a new journey' -- with a prediction that in ten years CJP will crown Azcuna 'The Consummate Hubby, Dad and Lolo,' even from a wheelchair.
